'''Beurre manié''', meaning "kneaded butter", is a paste made from equal volumes of butter and flour. It acts a thickener for soups and sauces.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Make French Beurre Manié to Thicken Soups and Sauces |url=https://www.thespruceeats.com/make-a-beurre-manie-1375421 |access-date=2024-11-29 |website=The Spruce Eats |language=en}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (60 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) softened [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
* ¼ cup (30 g) [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]

== Equipment ==
* [[Cookbook:Mixing bowl|Mixing bowl]]
 
== Procedure ==
# Combine the butter and flour in a mixing bowl.
# Use your hands or a small utensil such as a fork/spoon to knead the flour into the butter until fully and evenly incorporated.
# Use immediately or store as indicated in the notes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* To use it to thicken soups and sauces, whisk 2 tablespoons of the beurre manié into soups or sauces, then [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] until thickened.
* To freeze the beurre manié for long-term storage, portion it out into small balls (e.g. tablespoonfuls) and freeze until solid on a baking sheet. Transfer to an airtight ziplock bag, and store in the freezer for up to 3 months. Defrost completely before using.
